state.user_request_16_nov: Make each module MCP accessible. The user chose: render features via the Editor MCP, so masks, clip groups, track mattes, trim, fills, gradients and strokes can be set through scenes.edit, on the same command path as the Editor, refused by name.
facts: scenes.edit takes EditorCommand::EditScene { target, edits: Vec<SceneEdit> }; a batch is atomic and one undo entry. Today SceneEdit can set only 10 fields (opacity, x, y, rotation, scaleX, scaleY, text, fontId, size, radius) through SetObjectField, plus visibility, lock, keyframes, bindings and so on. Masks, clipChildId, trackMatte, trim, fill, stroke, strokeWidth and strokeStyle are authored scene fields (3.17 to 3.19) that no edit can set.

Every authoring write is a typed variant of one command type defined in Shared/contracts with generated TS and a JSON Schema per variant (11.36); no free-form property path exists, and the MCP author tier takes 11.36 commands only.

Existing edit style: SetObjectField validates a typed value, refuses an unknown object, an inapplicable kind (ObjectFieldNotApplicable) and an edit that changes nothing (ObjectFieldUnchanged), and returns EditEffect::ObjectsChanged.

drawability_refusals(document) is the one implementation of what the engine can draw; it already reports masks (MaskInvalid), clip groups (ClipGroupInvalid), track mattes (TrackMatteInvalid) and gradients (GradientNotDrawable) with a JSON path objects[i].field, and the validator and the engine both run it. Trim values are checked in validate.rs (ShapeTrimInvalid: start and end 0..100, offset finite).

Stroke style values (miterLimit at least 1, dash entries finite and not negative, at most 64 entries, a dash with length) are checked only by the engine when it prepares the stroke, so the Editor validator accepts a stroke style the engine later refuses.
A shape object has fillEnabled and strokeEnabled flags beside base.fill and base.stroke; a paint set while its flag is off draws nothing.
state.proposal: New SceneEdit variants: SetObjectMasks {objectId, masks: Vec<Mask>} (replaces the list; empty clears), SetClipChild {groupId, clipChildId: Option}, SetTrackMatte {objectId, trackMatte: Option}, SetTrim {objectId, start, end, offset: Option each, replacing all three}, SetPaint {objectIds, slot fill|stroke, paint: Option<ColorValue>}, SetStroke {objectIds, width, style: Option<StrokeStyle>}. Each validates after applying on the candidate by running drawability_refusals before and after and refusing on any refusal at the edited object or any refusal that was not there before; no new Refusal variant.

granularity.instructions: How should the render features be exposed for authoring?

criteria.typed_edits: One typed SceneEdit variant per feature (masks, clip child, track matte, trim, paint, stroke), each with its own schema and refusals.
criteria.generic_path: One generic set-property edit taking a JSON path and a JSON value, validated afterwards.

mask_list.instructions: How should an object's masks be edited?

criteria.replace_list: One edit replaces the object's whole mask list (empty clears it); an agent sends the list it wants and the batch is atomic.
criteria.per_mask_ops: Separate add, update, remove and reorder edits addressed by mask index.

validation.instructions: How should an edit refuse a value the engine cannot draw?

criteria.reuse_drawability: Run the existing drawability_refusals on the candidate scene before and after and refuse on any refusal at the edited object or any new refusal, so no rule is written twice.
criteria.per_edit_checks: Write the checks again inside each edit function.

stroke_style_checks.instructions: Where should the stroke style value checks live?

criteria.one_shared_function: One function in the contracts crate, called by SetStroke and by the engine's stroke preparation, so the edit and the engine refuse the same values.
criteria.engine_only: Leave them in the engine; SetStroke accepts any style and the engine refuses at publish.
criteria.copy_into_edit: Copy the checks into SetStroke and leave the engine's own.

shape_flags.instructions: What should SetPaint do to a shape's fillEnabled or strokeEnabled flag?

criteria.follow_paint: Set the flag on when a real paint is set and off when the paint is cleared or none, so the edit always draws what it says.
criteria.leave_flag: Leave the flag alone and accept that a paint on a disabled slot draws nothing.
criteria.refuse_when_off: Refuse the edit when the flag is off.

inapplicable_kinds.instructions: What should SetPaint, SetStroke and SetTrim do for an object kind that does not draw that paint, stroke or trim (a fill on a line, a stroke on a group, trim on a rect)?

criteria.refuse_by_name: Refuse with ObjectFieldNotApplicable naming the kinds, as SetObjectField does.
criteria.store_and_ignore: Store the value; the renderer ignores it.

needs_user.instructions: Must the user approve these before implementation?

criteria.true: Yes, a product choice is being made that the recorded user decisions do not cover.
criteria.false: No, these follow from the recorded decisions and the existing command model.
